## Local Foods & Traditional Dishes to Try in Toulouse and Occitanie

Toulouse and the wider Occitanie region are a paradise for food lovers, with a cuisine rooted in hearty, rustic traditions and high-quality local ingredients. Here are the must-try dishes and specialties:

---

### 🍲 Cassoulet de Toulouse
The quintessential dish of the region. This rich, slow-cooked stew combines **white beans** (ideally *haricots tarbais*), **duck confit**, **Toulouse sausage** (*saucisse de Toulouse*), pork belly, and aromatic broth. It's ubiquitous in Toulouse — nearly every traditional restaurant serves its own version.

### 🦆 Duck Confit (*Confit de Canard*)
An ancestral preservation technique where duck legs are slow-cooked in their own fat until meltingly tender. Duck is central to southwestern French cuisine, and confit de canard is a true symbol of the terroir. You'll also find **duck breast** (*magret de canard*) on many menus.

### 🍖 Saucisse de Toulouse
A celebrated pork sausage made according to traditional, artisanal methods. Only sausages produced in or near Toulouse following the authentic recipe may carry the full designation. It's a key ingredient in cassoulet but also delicious grilled on its own.

### 🫕 Foie Gras
The Gers department, just west of Toulouse, is one of France's premier foie gras–producing areas. Whether served as a block, mi-cuit, or pan-seared, duck and goose foie gras are iconic regional delicacies.

### 🥣 Garbure
A thick, hearty peasant soup from the Gascony area combining **cabbage, seasonal root vegetables, confit meat, and Tarbais beans**. It varies by season and cook — every version is different, and it's the ultimate comfort food of the southwest.

### 🧀 Aligot
A spectacular dish from the Aveyron area (within Occitanie): mashed potatoes blended with **fresh Tomme cheese, cream, and garlic** until incredibly stretchy and elastic. It's a must-try — head to a dedicated aligot restaurant for the full experience.

### 🧀 Roquefort
The famous blue cheese from the caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon in Aveyron, made from raw sheep's milk. A cornerstone of Occitanie's cheese heritage.

### 🧀 Pélardon
A small, soft goat's cheese from the Cévennes mountains in eastern Occitanie — delicate and tangy.

### 🍝 Gratin de Macaronis Toulousain
A comforting local take on baked pasta: macaroni in creamy béchamel sauce with Toulouse sausage and cheese.

### 💜 Violettes de Toulouse
Toulouse is famous for its violets, used in a surprising range of foods and drinks. The most iconic treat is **candied violet petals**, but you'll also find violet-flavored chocolates, liqueurs, and pastries. *La Maison de la Violette*, on a barge on the Canal du Midi, is the best place to explore these.

### 🍬 Cachou Lajaunie
A distinctive Toulouse confection — small liquorice-flavored pastilles that have been a local favorite for generations.

### 🦪 Oysters
Thanks to Toulouse's proximity to the Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts, fresh oysters are hugely popular, especially around the festive season.

### 🍷 Regional Wines & Drinks
Occitanie has been a wine-growing region for over 2,000 years. Look for **Corbières** reds, **Blanquette de Limoux** (one of the world's oldest sparkling wines), Gascony whites, and local **Armagnac** brandy.

---

Toulouse's **Marché Victor Hugo** is an excellent starting point to sample many of these specialties under one roof. Bon appétit!
